questions.text: What does LLM stand for in modern artificial intelligence?
questions.explanation: LLM stands for Large Language Model, a type of neural network trained on vast amounts of text.

questions.text: Which attention mechanism was introduced in the breakthrough paper "Attention Is All You Need"?
questions.explanation: Vaswani et al. (2017) introduced the Transformer architecture based on multi-head self-attention mechanisms.

questions.text: What is the primary role of "Temperature" in LLM text generation sampling?

options.text: Determines the randomness and diversity of token selection
Sets the maximum context window token length
Measures model confidence in raw percentage

questions.explanation: Temperature scales logits prior to softmax; lower values yield deterministic output while higher values increase randomness.

questions.text: What is RAG in contemporary enterprise AI architectures?
questions.explanation: Retrieval-Augmented Generation grounds LLMs with external authoritative documents before generating answers.

questions.text: Which vector database metric is most commonly used for dense embedding semantic similarity?
questions.explanation: Cosine similarity measures the cosine of the angle between two multi-dimensional dense vectors regardless of magnitude.

questions.text: What algorithm signal prioritizes content on modern feed-based social networks?
questions.explanation: High dwell time, active commenting, and shares are heavily weighted in distribution ranking algorithms.

questions.text: Which HTTP status code represents an unauthorized request requiring authentication?
questions.explanation: HTTP 401 denotes lack of valid authentication credentials for the target resource.

questions.text: What is the function of positional encoding in Transformer networks?

options.text: Encodes word sequence order into permutation-invariant attention
Compresses vocabulary size into byte-pair tokens
Encrypts embeddings against prompt injection attacks

questions.explanation: Since self-attention processes all tokens in parallel, positional encodings supply order information.

questions.text: What does RLHF stand for in large language model post-training?
questions.explanation: RLHF aligns raw base models with human preferences using reward models and PPO or DPO.

questions.text: Which quantization format reduces weights to 4 bits while preserving high task perplexity?
questions.explanation: Activation-aware Weight Quantization (AWQ) and GPTQ compress model weights to 4-bit integers efficiently.

questions.text: What does LoRA stand for in parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT)?
questions.explanation: LoRA freezes pretrained weights and injects trainable rank-decomposition matrices into transformer layers.

questions.text: What is the primary role of a System Prompt in instruction-tuned conversational models?

options.text: Establishes persistent behavioral persona and boundary constraints
Increases the clock frequency of the GPU memory
Calculates cosine similarity of output vectors
Converts English audio into Spanish subtitles

questions.explanation: System instructions define the model persona, tone, guidelines, and behavioral boundaries.

questions.text: What is the advantage of FlashAttention over vanilla self-attention implementations?

options.text: IO-awareness with tiling to avoid slow GPU High Bandwidth Memory reads
Removes the need for vector embeddings
Converts Python code into assembly language

questions.explanation: FlashAttention reorganizes attention computation into tiles stored in fast on-chip SRAM.

questions.text: What is "Hallucination" in the context of generative AI models?

options.text: Generating plausible-sounding but factually false or ungrounded assertions
A hardware overheating cycle on NVIDIA H100 servers
The compression phase of token serialization
Dropping TCP packets during WebSocket handshakes

questions.explanation: Hallucination occurs when a model produces confident output unsupported by factual reality.

questions.text: Which data structure is optimal for sub-millisecond Approximate Nearest Neighbor vector search?
questions.explanation: HNSW builds multi-layer proximity graphs providing logarithmic search times in dense vector spaces.

questions.text: In cloud computing, what does "Scale-to-Zero" mean for serverless deployments?

options.text: Container instances shut down when idle so costs drop to zero
Network bandwidth is throttled to 0 kbps
Hard drives erase all stored files automatically
Database tables drop all schema columns

questions.explanation: Scale-to-zero terminates idle compute instances, only spinning up when incoming traffic arrives.

questions.text: What is the purpose of CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) in browser web security?

options.text: Restricts web pages from requesting APIs from a different origin domain
Compresses JPEG photos into WebP format
Encrypts local hard drives with BitLocker

questions.explanation: CORS uses HTTP headers to tell browsers whether requests from other origins are allowed.

questions.text: Which protocol enables full-duplex, persistent two-way communication between client and server?
questions.explanation: WebSockets maintain open TCP connections allowing real-time bidirectional message exchange.

questions.text: What is the time complexity of looking up a key in a balanced Hash Map on average?
questions.explanation: Hash maps compute bucket indices via hashing functions, resulting in average O(1) retrieval.

questions.text: Which design pattern is used when a server notifies multiple subscribed clients of state changes?
questions.explanation: Publish-Subscribe (Pub-Sub) broadcasts events from publishers to all registered subscriber rooms.

questions.text: What does "Server-Authoritative Timing" prevent in real-time online games?

options.text: Cheating through client-side clock tampering and late answer spoofing
CSS styling bugs on mobile screens

questions.explanation: Server-authoritative timing enforces expiration based on the host server clock, ignoring tampered client timestamps.

questions.text: What is the main goal of Continuous Integration (CI) in modern DevOps pipelines?

options.text: Automating code builds, linting, and automated tests on every push
Manually emailing code zip files to production servers
Preventing developers from writing unit tests
Shutting down staging environments on weekends

questions.explanation: CI validates software changes continuously through automated build, type-check, and test suites.

questions.text: Which HTTP method is specifically idempotent for replacing a complete resource representation?
questions.explanation: HTTP PUT is idempotent; executing the identical PUT request multiple times leaves the server state identical.

questions.text: What is the purpose of JWT (JSON Web Token) signatures in stateless authentication?

options.text: Ensures the payload has not been tampered with by clients or intermediaries
Encrypts the token so nobody can read the payload fields
Stores database passwords in plain text

questions.explanation: Cryptographic HMAC or RSA signatures allow verifying token authenticity without database lookups.

questions.text: In distributed databases, what does the CAP theorem state is impossible to guarantee simultaneously in a partition?
questions.explanation: During a network partition, distributed systems must choose between Consistency or Availability.

questions.text: What is the purpose of Docker containerization in software deployment?

options.text: Packages application code with all dependencies into immutable, portable images
Replaces the Linux operating system kernel with Python
Doubles the physical RAM of motherboard slots
Monitors user keystrokes in background threads

questions.explanation: Containers package dependencies and code together so apps run reliably across any cloud environment.

questions.text: What is the primary role of Redis in high-throughput real-time web applications?

options.text: In-memory key-value caching and sub-millisecond pub/sub message brokering
Rendering 3D graphic models in the browser

questions.explanation: Redis keeps data in RAM, serving millions of operations per second with microsecond latencies.

questions.text: True or False: In JavaScript, typeof null returns "object".
questions.explanation: This is a historic bug in JS dating back to 1995 where values with type tag 0 were flagged as objects.

questions.text: True or False: HTTP/2 requires multiple TCP connections to transmit parallel asset streams.
questions.explanation: HTTP/2 introduces multiplexing over a single TCP connection.

questions.text: True or False: React useEffect without a dependency array runs only once after the initial render.
questions.explanation: Without a dependency array, useEffect runs after EVERY render. An empty array [] runs once on mount.

questions.text: True or False: In relational databases, a PRIMARY KEY column automatically enforces NOT NULL constraint.
questions.explanation: A primary key column must contain unique values and cannot contain NULL values.

questions.text: True or False: CSS Flexbox is designed primarily for 2-dimensional layouts (both rows and columns simultaneously).
questions.explanation: Flexbox is 1-dimensional (row OR column). CSS Grid is designed for 2-dimensional grid layouts.

questions.text: True or False: Symmetric encryption algorithms use the exact same secret key for both encryption and decryption.
questions.explanation: Symmetric ciphers like AES use one shared key; asymmetric ciphers (RSA/ECC) use public/private key pairs.

questions.text: What will this print? [1, 2, 3].map(parseInt)
questions.explanation: parseInt takes (string, radix). map passes (element, index). Index 0 is default radix 10, index 1 is radix 1 (invalid => NaN), index 2 is radix 2 ("3" is invalid binary => NaN).

questions.text: In Python: what is the result of bool([] == False)?
questions.explanation: While bool([]) is False, an empty list does not equal False in value comparison ([] == False is False).

questions.text: What is the worst-case runtime complexity of Quicksort when using a naive first-element pivot on sorted data?
questions.explanation: On sorted arrays with first-element pivot, partitioning degenerates into N recursive calls of size N-1, yielding O(N^2).

questions.text: In SQL: SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(col) FROM t. When will COUNT(*) be greater than COUNT(col)?

options.text: When col is a PRIMARY KEY

questions.explanation: COUNT(*) counts all rows including NULLs; COUNT(column) ignores rows where column is NULL.

questions.text: What does the following Git command do? git cherry-pick <commit-hash>

options.text: Applies the changes from an existing commit onto the current HEAD branch
Deletes the commit permanently from git history
Reverts the commit with an inverse commit

questions.explanation: git cherry-pick takes the patch introduced by a specific commit and creates a new commit on the active branch.

questions.text: What port number does HTTPS use by default?
questions.explanation: Port 443 is the standard port for TLS/HTTPS traffic.

questions.text: Which company created the Go (Golang) programming language?
questions.explanation: Go was designed at Google in 2007 by Robert Griesemer, Rob Pike, and Ken Thompson.

questions.text: What is the name of GitHub package registry manager for JavaScript and TypeScript?
questions.explanation: npm (Node Package Manager) is the default registry for Node.js.

questions.text: What does DNS stand for in computer networking?
questions.explanation: DNS translates human-readable domain names (like example.com) to machine IP addresses.

questions.text: Which company developed the React library?
questions.explanation: React was created by Jordan Walke, a software engineer at Meta.

questions.text: What cloud computing service model provides virtualized servers, storage, and networking?
questions.explanation: IaaS provides bare compute, disk, and networking instances (e.g. AWS EC2, GCP Compute Engine).

questions.text: Which SQL clause is used to filter aggregated grouped records?
questions.explanation: WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters the groups produced by GROUP BY.

questions.text: What type of attack involves injecting malicious scripts into trusted websites viewed by other users?
questions.explanation: XSS executes attacker scripts in victim browsers through unescaped user-supplied inputs.

questions.text: Which metric is the best evaluation for an imbalanced fraud detection classifier?
questions.explanation: Accuracy is misleading for 99.9% negative classes; PR-AUC and F1-score evaluate true positive recovery.

questions.text: What is the primary benefit of GraphQL over REST APIs?

options.text: Clients query exact fields needed, preventing over-fetching and under-fetching
GraphQL operates without an HTTP transport layer
It completely eliminates the need for a database
It compresses all server responses into binary zip files

questions.explanation: GraphQL lets the client declare exact field shapes in one roundtrip request.

questions.text: Which of the following is explicitly listed as a process scheduling algorithm in the curriculum?
questions.explanation: The document states: 'Process Scheduling (Round Robin, FIFO)'.

questions.text: What is the full form of TLB as mentioned in the curriculum?
questions.explanation: The document explicitly defines the term: 'TLB Translation Lookaside Buffer'.

questions.text: According to the curriculum, which tools are used for synchronization?
questions.explanation: The document states: 'Semaphores, and Mutex Locks for synchronization.'
